person: Ida Marsh, farm girl and newspaper editor, born 1941 (made up)
summary: A whole life, but the memories arrive shuffled, the member hasn't chosen a kind of book, and hasn't said who it's for. The agent should suggest a life memoir and put the chapters back in time order itself.

memories.title: Editor
memories.body: Mr. Dahl retired and handed me the keys to the Courier. I was the first woman to edit it. The first letter to the editor that week asked if I could also do something about the potholes.

memories.title: Snowed in for nine days
memories.body: In January the snow drifted over the kitchen windows and we were snowed in for nine days. Mother taught me to make bread and play gin rummy. I won forty-two games.

memories.title: The front-page quilt
memories.body: Started a quilt from Courier front pages printed on fabric. Forty squares, one for every year that mattered. It took four winters.

memories.title: The typing pool in Merriton
memories.body: Took a job in the typing pool at Great Plains Mutual in Merriton. Sixty-two words a minute. The supervisor, Miss Kraus, timed us with a kitchen timer.

memories.title: Furnace filter
memories.body: Changed the furnace filter. Next one due in March. 16x25x1.

memories.title: Last issue
memories.body: Printed my last issue as editor after twenty-three years. The staff hid a fake front page in the bundle: IDA MARSH RETIRES, COUNTY IN SHOCK.

memories.title: Haying with Grandpa Ott
memories.body: I rode on the hay wagon while Grandpa Ott forked bales. He told me the clouds' names: cumulus, nimbus, and one he made up called Ida's sheep.

memories.title: The Courier's want ad
memories.body: The Brindle Courier needed someone to type up the county news. I applied on a Tuesday and was writing the obituaries by Friday.

memories.title: Ida's sheep, again
memories.body: My great-grandson rode the hay wagon at the county fair and I told him the clouds' names, including Ida's sheep. He believed every word.

memories.title: The schoolhouse closes
memories.body: The one-room school on the Coldwater road closed and we were bused to town. I hated the bus and loved the library, which had more books than our whole county.

memories.title: Running for council
memories.body: Ran for county council at fifty-eight because nobody else would fix the Coldwater road. Won by thirty-one votes. Fixed the road.

memories.title: Coming home
memories.body: Father's back gave out and I came home to help with the farm. I thought it would be for one harvest. It was for the rest of my life, more or less.

memories.title: The elevator fire
memories.body: The co-op grain elevator burned on a Sunday night. I took photographs until four in the morning and we put out a special edition by noon. It's the only time the Courier ever sold out.

cases.about: Memories arrive out of order; no book type, no audience. Expect a life memoir, told in time order.
